## Findings

I searched Home State Health's and Ambetter Health's published Clinical & Payment Policy library (the "CP.MP.XX" policy manual) that governs prior-authorization/medical-necessity decisions for this plan, and I could not find a plan-specific medical policy for hallux valgus correction / bunionectomy (CPT 28296) or "foot surgery" generally. The alphabetical policy index on the Home State Health / Ambetter provider site (which lists every CP.MP policy by name, e.g., between "Fetal Surgery" and "Foster Care," and between "Bariatric Surgery" and "Burn Surgery") has no entry for Bunionectomy, Hallux Valgus, or Foot Surgery.

This appears to be intentional, not a gap in my search: Home State Health's own provider "Quality Care" page states that "**Nationally recognized criteria (such as InterQual or MCG) are used if available for the specific service request, without additional criteria (e.g., clinical/medical policies) developed internally**..." and the parallel Ambetter Health clinical-policy pages for sister Centene plans state that the plan "**utilizes InterQual® criteria for those medical technologies, procedures or pharmaceutical treatments for which a [plan] clinical policy does not exist**." Bunionectomy/hallux valgus surgery falls in that category for this plan — there is no published Home State Health/Ambetter medical policy document; the actual criteria applied are almost certainly a licensed, non-public InterQual® (or MCG®) criteria set (e.g., InterQual CP: Procedures – "Correction, Hallux Valgus with Bunionectomy" or similar), which Centene/Ambetter does not post publicly because it is copyrighted third-party content.

I did confirm the plan's appeals process and address/deadline from Ambetter's own Appeals/Reconsiderations & Grievances Guide (Missouri, last updated October 2024).

**Practical next step for the appeal:** Since the underlying clinical criteria aren't public, the appeal letter should (a) formally request the specific medical-necessity criteria/guideline used in this denial, and (b) in the meantime, address the standard elements virtually every payer's bunionectomy criteria require regardless of which proprietary tool is used — documented symptomatic hallux valgus with radiographic angle measurements (hallux valgus angle / intermetatarsal angle), a defined trial (commonly 3–6 months) of conservative treatment (padding, wider/orthopedic shoes, orthotics, NSAIDs, activity modification) that has failed, and objective functional impairment/pain limiting activities of daily living — supported by the surgeon's exam notes, weight-bearing X-rays, and conservative-care records, since these are the elements InterQual/MCG-type foot-surgery criteria typically require and are the most defensible basis for arguing medical necessity even before the exact criteria document is produced.
